Class DialogFrame

java.lang.Object
io.mcs.taskmanager.ui.DialogFrame
final class DialogFrame extends Object
What every dialog sits in: the dimmed window, and a white card with the dialog's title, note, fields, the reason a save was refused, and Cancel and the main button at its foot. Enter saves from a one-line field, Ctrl+Enter from anywhere in the dialog, and Escape cancels.
Author:
Hamza Rasool, Abdullah Khan

  • Method Details

    • overlay

      javafx.scene.Node overlay()
      The dimmed layer with the card on it, for the window to lay over everything else.
      Returns:
      the layer

    • focus

      void focus()
      Puts the keyboard where the dialog starts: its first field, or the card itself for a question. The layer's stylesheet is applied first: until then the scroll pane has no skin, so the card is not yet in the window and could not take the focus.

    • holds

      boolean holds(javafx.scene.Node node)
      Whether a node is part of the dialog, so the window can keep the keyboard inside it.
      Parameters:
      node - the node that has the focus
      Returns:
      true if it is the card or anything in it

    • draw

      private void draw()
      Lays out the card afresh: the heading, the fields, the refusal if there is one, and the buttons.

    • save

      private void save()
      Saves through the dialog. A refusal stays in the dialog under its fields, except that a task which has gone closes it and is reported over the list, where it has disappeared. A failure nobody expected is written to the log and shown as a plain sentence, never as an error's trace.

    • refuse

      private void refuse(String reason)
      Shows why a save did not happen under the fields, and puts the keyboard back in the first of them.
      Parameters:
      reason - the sentence to show
